title_en: Implementing Regulations of the Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Individual Income Tax Law).

Article 2 For the purposes of the Individual Income Tax Law, the term 'domicile within the territory of China' means habitual residence within the territory of China due to household registration, family, or economic interests; the term 'income derived from within and outside the territory of China' means income sourced from within the territory of China and income sourced from outside the territory of China, respectively.

Article 4 For an individual who has no domicile within the territory of China but has resided in China for an aggregate of 183 days in a tax year, if the consecutive years of such residence are less than six years, and upon filing with the competent tax authorities, the income derived from outside China and paid by an entity or individual outside China shall be exempted from individual income tax; if in any tax year in which the individual has resided in China for an aggregate of 183 days, there is a departure from China exceeding 30 days, the consecutive years of residence in China for an aggregate of 183 days shall be recalculated.

Article 5 For an individual who has no domicile within the territory of China and who has resided in China for an aggregate of no more than 90 days in a tax year, the portion of income derived from within the territory of China that is paid by an overseas employer and not borne by the establishment or place of business of such employer within the territory of China shall be exempted from individual income tax.

Article 6 The scope of various categories of individual income as provided for in the Individual Income Tax Law:
(1) Income from wages and salaries means the income obtained by an individual from wages, salaries, bonuses, year-end bonuses, labor dividends, allowances, subsidies, and other income related to employment or engagement.
(2) Income from remuneration for labor services means income obtained by an individual from providing labor services, including income from design, decoration, installation, drafting, laboratory testing, medical services, legal services, accounting, consulting, lecturing, translation, manuscript review, painting and calligraphy, sculpture, film and television, recording, video recording, performances, shows, advertising, exhibitions, technical services, introduction services, brokerage services, agency services, and other labor services.
(3) Income from author's remuneration means income obtained by an individual from the publication or distribution of his or her works in the form of books, newspapers, periodicals, etc.
(4) Income from royalties means income obtained by an individual from the provision of the right to use patent rights, trademark rights, copyrights, non-patented technology, and other franchise rights; income from the provision of the right to use copyrights shall not include income from author's remuneration.
(5) Income from business operations means:
1. income obtained by individual industrial and commercial households from production and business operations, and income obtained by investors in sole proprietorship enterprises and individual partners in partnerships from production and business operations of sole proprietorship enterprises and partnerships registered within the territory of China;
2. income obtained by individuals from engaging in education, medical services, consulting, and other paid service activities in accordance with law;
3. income obtained by individuals from contracting, leasing, sub-contracting, and sub-leasing of enterprises and public institutions;
4. income obtained by individuals from other production and business operations.
(6) Income from interest, dividends, and bonuses means income from interest, dividends, and bonuses obtained by an individual by virtue of owning creditor's rights, equity interests, etc.
(7) Income from property leasing means income obtained by an individual from leasing real property, machinery and equipment, vehicles and vessels, and other property.
(8) Income from property transfer means income obtained by an individual from transferring marketable securities, equity interests, property shares in partnerships, real property, machinery and equipment, vehicles and vessels, and other property.
(9) Incidental income means income obtained by an individual from winning awards, prizes, lotteries, and other incidental income.
For income obtained by an individual that is difficult to determine the taxable item, the competent tax department of the State Council shall determine it.

Article 7 The measures for the collection of individual income tax on income from the transfer of shares shall be separately prescribed by the State Council and filed with the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for the record.

Article 8 Forms of individual income include cash, physical objects, negotiable securities, and other forms of economic benefits. If the income is in the form of physical objects, the taxable income amount shall be calculated based on the price indicated on the voucher obtained; if there is no voucher or the price indicated on the voucher is obviously low, the taxable income amount shall be determined by reference to the market price. If the income is in the form of negotiable securities, the taxable income amount shall be determined based on the face value and market price. If the income is in the form of other economic benefits, the taxable income amount shall be determined by reference to the market price.

Article 9 The term 'interest on national bonds' as mentioned in Item (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 4 of the Individual Income Tax Law means interest obtained by an individual from holding bonds issued by the Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China; the term 'interest on financial bonds issued by the state' means interest obtained by an individual from holding financial bonds approved for issuance by the State Council.

Article 10 The term 'allowances and subsidies granted in accordance with uniform state regulations' as mentioned in Item (3) of Paragraph 1 of Article 4 of the Individual Income Tax Law means the government special allowances, academician allowances granted in accordance with the regulations of the State Council, and other allowances and subsidies exempted from individual income tax as prescribed by the State Council.

Article 11. The welfare fees referred to in Item 4 of Paragraph 1 of Article 4 of the Individual Income Tax Law means the living subsidies paid to individuals from the welfare fees or trade union funds set aside by enterprises, public institutions, state organs, and social organizations in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State; the relief funds referred to therein means the living hardship subsidies paid to individuals by the civil affairs departments of the people's governments at all levels.

Article 12. The income of diplomatic representatives, consular officers, and other personnel of foreign embassies and consulates in China that shall be exempted from tax in accordance with relevant laws as referred to in Item 8 of Paragraph 1 of Article 4 of the Individual Income Tax Law means the income exempted from tax in accordance with the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities and the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Consular Privileges and Immunities.

Article 13. The other deductions determined according to law as referred to in Item 1 of Paragraph 1 of Article 6 of the Individual Income Tax Law include: contributions made by individuals to enterprise annuities and occupational annuities that comply with state regulations, expenditures for the purchase by individuals of commercial health insurance and tax-deferred commercial endowment insurance that comply with state regulations, and other items that the State Council stipulates may be deducted.
Special deductions, special additional deductions, and other deductions determined according to law shall be limited by the taxable income of a resident individual for a tax year; if the deductions are not fully utilized in a tax year, they shall not be carried forward to subsequent tax years.

Article 14. The term "each instance" as referred to in Items 2, 4, and 6 of Paragraph 1 of Article 6 of the Individual Income Tax Law shall be determined separately according to the following methods:
(1) For income from remuneration for personal services, income from author's remuneration, and income from royalties, if it is a one-time income, the receipt of such income shall be deemed as one instance; if it is a continuous income from the same project, the income received within one month shall be deemed as one instance.
(2) For income from property leasing, the income received within one month shall be deemed as one instance.
(3) For income from interest, dividends, and bonuses, the income received at the time of payment of interest, dividends, or bonuses shall be deemed as one instance.
(4) For incidental income, each receipt of such income shall be deemed as one instance.

Article 15. The term "costs and expenses" as referred to in Item 3 of Paragraph 1 of Article 6 of the Individual Income Tax Law means various direct expenditures incurred in production and business activities, indirect expenses allocated to costs, as well as selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses; the term "losses" means inventory losses, damages, and abandonment losses of fixed assets and inventories incurred in production and business activities, losses from transfer of property, bad debt losses, losses caused by force majeure factors such as natural disasters, and other losses.
For an individual who obtains income from business operations but does not have comprehensive income, when calculating the taxable income for each tax year, expenses of 60,000 yuan, special deductions, special additional deductions, and other deductions determined according to law shall be deducted. Special additional deductions shall be deducted when handling the annual settlement.
If an individual engaged in production and business activities fails to provide complete and accurate tax records and cannot correctly calculate the taxable income, the competent tax authority shall assess the taxable income or the amount of tax payable.

Article 17. For income from transfer of property, tax shall be calculated on the balance after deducting the original value of the property and reasonable expenses from the income from a single transfer of property.

Article 18. Where two or more individuals jointly obtain income from the same project, tax shall be calculated separately for the income obtained by each individual in accordance with the provisions of the Individual Income Tax Law.

Article 19. The phrase "an individual donates his or her income to public welfare and charitable undertakings such as education, poverty alleviation, and relief" as referred to in Paragraph 3 of Article 6 of the Individual Income Tax Law means donations made by an individual through public welfare social organizations or state organs within the territory of China to public welfare and charitable undertakings such as education, poverty alleviation, and relief; the term "taxable income" referred to therein means the taxable income before calculating the deduction of the donation amount.

Article 20. For comprehensive income and income from business operations obtained by a resident individual from within and outside China, the tax payable shall be calculated on a consolidated basis separately; for other income obtained from within and outside China, the tax payable shall be calculated separately on an individual basis.

Article 21 The amount of individual income tax that has been paid outside China as referred to in Article 7 of the Individual Income Tax Law means the amount of income tax that a resident individual shall pay and has actually paid in accordance with the law of the country (region) where the income originates from outside China.
The amount of tax payable calculated in accordance with the provisions of this Law on the income of a taxpayer from outside China as referred to in Article 7 of the Individual Income Tax Law is the limit (hereinafter referred to as the tax credit limit) for a resident individual to offset the amount of income tax that has been paid outside China on comprehensive income, business income and other income. Unless otherwise provided by the competent departments of finance and taxation under the State Council, the sum of the tax credit limit for comprehensive income, the tax credit limit for business income and the tax credit limit for other income from a country (region) outside China shall be the tax credit limit for income from that country (region).
Where the amount of individual income tax that a resident individual has actually paid in a country (region) outside China is lower than the tax credit limit for income from that country (region) calculated in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the difference shall be paid in China; where it exceeds the tax credit limit for income from that country (region), the excess part shall not be offset against the tax payable for the current tax year, but may be recouped from the balance of the tax credit limit for income from that country (region) in subsequent tax years. The recoupment period shall not exceed five years.

Article 22 If a resident individual applies for a tax credit for the amount of individual income tax that has been paid outside China, the resident individual shall provide relevant tax payment vouchers for the tax year in question issued by the tax authority of the country outside China.

Article 23 The interest as specified in paragraph 2 of Article 8 of the Individual Income Tax Law shall be calculated based on the benchmark loan interest rate for the same period in RMB published by the People's Bank of China on the last day of the tax declaration period to which the tax underpayment relates, and shall be charged on a daily basis from the day after the expiration of the tax declaration period until the expiration of the tax supplementary payment period. Where the taxpayer pays the tax before the expiration of the tax supplementary payment period, the interest shall be charged until the day of payment.

Article 24 When a withholding agent pays taxable amounts to an individual, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Individual Income Tax Law, withhold or deduct the tax, pay it into the treasury on time, and maintain special records for future inspection.
The term "payment" as mentioned in the preceding paragraph includes cash payment, remittance payment, transfer payment, and payment in the form of securities, physical objects, and other forms.

Article 26 The term "full-staff full-amount withholding declaration" as referred to in paragraph 2 of Article 10 of the Individual Income Tax Law means that the withholding agent shall, within fifteen days of the month following the month in which the tax is withheld, submit to the competent tax authority the relevant information of all individuals to whom payments are made, the amount of payments made, deduction items and amounts, the specific amount and total amount of tax withheld, and other relevant tax-related information.
Article 27 The specific measures for the place of tax filing by taxpayers and other related matters shall be formulated by the competent tax authority under the State Council.

Article 28 When a resident individual derives income from wages and salaries, the resident individual may provide the withholding agent with information concerning special additional deductions, and the withholding agent shall deduct the special additional deductions when withholding the tax. Where the taxpayer derives income from wages and salaries from two or more sources at the same time and the withholding agent deducts the special additional deductions, for the same special additional deduction item, the deduction may only be taken against income derived from one source within a tax year.
A resident individual who derives income from remuneration for personal services, author's remuneration, or royalties shall provide the relevant information to the tax authority when conducting the annual settlement and deduct the special additional deductions.
Article 29 A taxpayer may entrust a withholding agent or another entity or individual to handle the annual settlement.

Article 30 A withholding agent shall calculate and handle the withholding declaration based on the information provided by the taxpayer, and shall not unilaterally change the information provided by the taxpayer.
Where a taxpayer discovers that the personal information, income, tax withheld, etc. provided by the withholding agent or declared by the withholding agent are inconsistent with the actual circumstances, the taxpayer has the right to request the withholding agent to make corrections. If the withholding agent refuses to make corrections, the taxpayer shall report to the tax authority, which shall handle the matter in a timely manner.
Taxpayers and withholding agents shall retain the materials related to special additional deductions as required. The tax authority may conduct random checks on the information concerning special additional deductions provided by the taxpayer, and the specific measures shall be separately formulated by the competent tax authority under the State Council. Where the tax authority finds that a taxpayer has provided false information, it shall order the taxpayer to make corrections and notify the withholding agent; if the circumstances are serious, the relevant authorities shall handle the matter according to law, include the information in the credit information system, and implement joint disciplinary measures.

Article 31 Where the information on the annual reconciliation provided by a taxpayer when applying for tax refund is erroneous, the tax authority shall notify the taxpayer to make corrections; if the taxpayer makes corrections, the tax authority shall handle the tax refund in a timely manner.
Where a withholding agent fails to turn over the withheld tax to the State treasury, it shall not affect the taxpayer's right to apply for a tax refund in accordance with the provisions, and the tax authority shall handle the tax refund based on the relevant materials provided by the taxpayer.

Article 32 Where the income is in a currency other than Renminbi, the taxable income shall be computed by converting it into Renminbi at the central parity rate of Renminbi on the last day of the month preceding the month in which the tax return or withholding return is filed. Where annual reconciliation is handled after the end of the year, the income in a currency other than Renminbi on which tax has been prepaid on a monthly, quarterly or per-transaction basis shall not be converted again; for the part of income for which tax shall be made up, the taxable income shall be computed by converting it into Renminbi at the central parity rate of Renminbi on the last day of the preceding tax year.

Article 33 Where the tax authority pays handling fees to a withholding agent in accordance with the provisions of Article 17 of the Individual Income Tax Law, it shall issue a refund certificate; the withholding agent shall, based on the refund certificate, go through the procedures for refunding the fees into the treasury in accordance with the relevant provisions on treasury management.

Article 34 The formats of the individual income tax return, the withholding individual income tax report, and the individual income tax payment certificate shall be uniformly formulated by the tax authority of the State Council.
Article 35 The collection of individual income tax on military personnel shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions.
Article 36 These Regulations shall come into force as of January 1, 2019.
